rounds.text: Delhivery Ltd demonstrates robust top-line momentum, with compounded sales growth over 5 years and the trailing twelve months both printing at a strong 24% [E14, E16]. This commercial expansion is successfully translating into bottom-line acceleration, evidenced by a 52% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and quarterly net profit surging 182% year-over-year [E19, E61]. Operational efficiency is structurally improving, marked by a multi-year increasing operating-margin trend [E27], a 7% TTM operating margin representing a 5 percentage point expansion over three years [E25], and working capital requirements dramatically shrinking from 71.1 days down to 37.2 days [E53]. Furthermore, the business is exceptionally cash-generative, delivering Rs 911 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 506 Cr in free cash flow for March 2026 [E30, E31], underpinned by an impressive 5.95x cash conversion rate that proves reported profits are fully backed by hard cash [E29]. The balance sheet remains a pillar of strength with a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.15x and comfortable short-term liquidity through a 2.59x current ratio [E32, E33], while institutional confidence is clearly rotating toward domestic heavyweights who now hold 45.95% [E37] alongside positive overall institutional money flow [E38]. Conceded: [E6], [E39], [E56], [E65].

The valuation of Delhivery Ltd is severely disconnected from reality, trading at a staggering P/E ratio of 163x [E1] and an exorbitant 184.72x against a sector benchmark of just 17.91x [E6]. This extreme multiple is completely unsupported by fundamental profitability, as evidenced by a miserable ROE of -0.2% [E13], a median 5-year ROE of -6% [E22], and an anemic ROCE of only 1.0% [E12]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow analysis places intrinsic value at a mere Rs 75 per share compared to the market price of Rs 457 [E39], resulting in an alarming margin of safety of -508.2% [E40]. To justify today's share price, the company would need to deliver an unrealistic 39.7% earnings growth rate, vastly outstripping the base case assumption of 14.0% [E41]. Compounding these fundamental vulnerabilities, foreign institutional investors have aggressively slashed their holdings from 62.71% in December 2023 to 39.54% in September 2026 [E36], signalling a massive loss of confidence among sophisticated market participants. Conceded: [E14], [E25], [E30], [E31], [E32].

The bear’s reliance on historical P/E and ROE metrics ignores the company’s rapid operational transformation, where profit growth has accelerated to 52% in the trailing twelve months [E19] and quarterly operating margins have expanded by 4 percentage points year-over-year [E26]. While the bear cites low historical ROE [E13, E22], it fails to account for the structural improvement in working capital requirements, which have plummeted from 71.1 days to 37.2 days, signaling a shift toward higher efficiency [E53]. The DCF valuation [E39, E40] is a static model that fails to capture the momentum of a business currently generating Rs 911 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 506 Cr in free cash flow [E30, E31]. The reduction in foreign institutional holdings [E36] is more than offset by a massive 28.93 percentage point increase in domestic institutional ownership [E37], reflecting a fundamental shift in the investor base toward those closer to the company's domestic growth story. Conceded: [E1], [E6], [E12], [E13], [E22], [E36], [E39], [E40], [E41]. The current price reflects a market pricing in the company's proven ability to outperform expectations, as profit growth currently exceeds one-year price growth by 39% [E51].

Conceded: [E19], [E26], [E53]. While the bull points to recent profit growth and operating margin expansion [E19, E26], it glosses over the fact that current earnings are artificially inflated by Rs 303 Cr of other income [E57]. The bull's dismissal of the DCF valuation as static ignores the reverse DCF reality that the current price already aggressively prices in 39.7% earnings growth against a base case of just 14.0% [E41]. Conceded: [E30], [E31], [E37]. Although operating and free cash flows look robust at Rs 911 Cr and Rs 506 Cr respectively [E30, E31], domestic institutional inflows [E37] do not erase the massive foreign institutional exit from 62.71% down to 39.54% [E36]. Furthermore, the bull’s argument that profits exceed price growth by 39% [E51] relies on a trailing momentum metric that fails to justify an extreme P/E of 163x [E1] and a negative -508.2% margin of safety [E40].
